Italian Feast of the Seven Fishes

Served at: Christmas Eve

Serves 6Prep 45 minCook 1 hr 30 min

The Feast of the Seven Fishes is a traditional Italian-American Christmas Eve celebration featuring seven different seafood dishes. This meal honors the vigil before Christmas Day and showcases a variety of flavors from the sea, symbolizing abundance and good fortune for the coming year.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) calamari, cleaned and sliced into rings
  • 1 lb (450 g) large shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • 1 lb (450 g) mussels, cleaned
  • 1 lb (450 g) clams, cleaned
  • 1 lb (450 g) cod fillets, cut into chunks
  • 1/2 lb (225 g) scallops
  • 1/2 lb (225 g) smelt or whitebait
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dry white wine
  • 1 can (14 oz/400 g) crushed tomatoes
  • 1/4 cup (10 g) fresh parsley, chopped
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • 1 lb (450 g) spaghetti or linguine
  • Lemon wedges, for serving

Method

  1. Rinse all seafood under cold water and pat dry.
  2. In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté garlic and red pepper flakes until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
  3. Add crushed tomatoes and white wine to the pot, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes to develop flavors.
  4. Add the cod chunks and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
  5. Add calamari, shrimp, scallops, and smelt; cook for 5 minutes until seafood begins to turn opaque.
  6. Add mussels and clams, cover the pot, and cook for 5-7 minutes until shells open. Discard any unopened shells.
  7. Season the sauce with salt, pepper, and chopped parsley; keep warm on low heat.
  8. Meanwhile, cook spaghetti or linguine according to package instructions until al dente; drain and reserve some pasta water.
  9. Toss the pasta with the seafood sauce, adding reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
  10. Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

Tips

  • Feel free to vary the types of seafood based on availability and preference, but aim for seven different kinds to honor tradition.
  • Use fresh seafood whenever possible for the best flavor and texture.
  • Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the delicious sauce.
